  PROBLEM: The comment says the loop captures the "oldest" matching merge commit, but `git log` without `--reverse` is newest-first, so the first subject-ending match is actually the newest commit.
  WHY: If more than one commit ends with the same `(#<pr>)` suffix, the helper can use the wrong `merge_unix` and purge or keep the wrong fingerprint state.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:2166-2170 | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The same `git log` ordering comment says "oldest" even though the loop sees newest-first output, so it records the newest matching commit instead.
  WHY: With duplicated `(#<pr>)` suffixes, the wrong timestamp can drive stale/healthy purge decisions.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:2196-2200 | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: `any_ref=1` is set for any `git log --grep` hit, even when the subject does not end with `(#<pr>)`, so the flag does not actually mean a merge commit was found.
  WHY: The name/semantics can mislead maintainers even though the temporal guard still prevents an incorrect purge.
- tests/test_fingerprint_state_selfheal.py:33 | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: `_iso()` imports `datetime` inside the function body rather than at module scope.
  WHY: It works at runtime, but it is unidiomatic and adds per-call import overhead.
- tests/test_fingerprint_state_selfheal.py:144 | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: `_run_heal` is defined but never called by any test in the file.
  WHY: The helper is dead code and its parsed post-state return value is never exercised.
- tests/test_fingerprint_state_selfheal.py:144 | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The test file's helper flow depends on writable `/tmp`/`TemporaryDirectory`, and `main()` reports 0/11 passed in the current CI/sandbox context.
  WHY: The suite does not execute reliably, so regressions in the purge predicates go undetected.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:2149-2190 | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Missing/invalid inputs and malformed timestamps or jq failures are handled by silent early returns or empty-string keeps, so stale entries can remain without diagnostics.
  WHY: Operators only see the downstream gate failure, not why self-heal skipped the entry.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:2201-2203 | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: `date -u -d` parse failures and jq errors are swallowed, leaving malformed state entries in place.
  WHY: Corrupt or legacy entries persist and the gate continues hard-failing with no operator signal.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:2182-2193 | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: Entries with non-numeric `pr` values are `continue`d forever, even if stale.
  WHY: Corrupted or legacy stale entries can persist indefinitely.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:2203-2228 | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The helper rewrites `STATE_FILE` per deletion via `jq ... > tmp && mv` without a backup or lock, so interruption or overlapping pollers can leave `merged_issue_fingerprints` partially purged or corrupted.
  WHY: The workflow concurrency guard does not protect the in-process file rewrite, so the self-heal is not interruption-safe.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:~14370 | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `_purge_stale_fingerprint_entries_on_integration_branch` rewrites the state file via `jq del > tmp && mv` with no backup or lock, so a crash or SIGTERM can leave partial state.
  WHY: The self-heal is not fully idempotent under interruption.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:2185-2190 | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Each deleted entry triggers a full `jq` parse/serialize/write of the state file, making the purge loop quadratic in the number of stale entries.
  WHY: It does unnecessary I/O/CPU churn; a single-pass delete would be linear.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:14385-14388 | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `::warning::FINGERPRINT_STATE_SELFHEAL_V1` and the `## 🩹 Integration fingerprint state self-heal` marker were introduced without updating the stable log-prefix contract.
  WHY: Downstream log-analysis, drift-audit, and Telegram/other consumers that key on the registered prefix list can miss or misclassify these events.
- agents.md:185-203 | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: `FINGERPRINT_STATE_SELFHEAL_V1` is not registered in the stable log prefixes list.
  WHY: The documented stable-prefix contract will not recognize self-heal events, so downstream tooling can miss or misclassify them.
